\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{أدرك} (adraka)}{أدرك (adraka)}]{\ar{أدرك} (adraka) — to realize}

\label{lesson:AR-C367-adraka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to believe someone, then the Arabic for to infer.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{أدرك}}
\textbf{\ar{أدرك}} — \emph{adraka} — \textquotedblleft{}to realize\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{أدركت} \ar{أنني} \ar{نسيت} \ar{مفتاحي}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{adraktu annanī nasītu miftāḥī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I realized that I had forgotten my key.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يدرك}, \emph{yudrik}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{أدرك}} (\emph{adraka}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{d-r-k}, \textquotedblleft{}to overtake, to reach\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form IV, to catch up with: a thought catches up with you, and you realize.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{adraka}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{adraka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{adraktu annanī nasītu miftāḥī.} — I realized that I had forgotten my key.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to believe someone, then the Arabic for to infer, then say \emph{adraka} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{أدرك} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To realize\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تصور} (taṣawwara)}{تصور (taṣawwara)}]{\ar{تصور} (taṣawwara) — to conceive}

\label{lesson:AR-C367-tasawwara}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to infer, then the Arabic for to realize.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تصور}}
\textbf{\ar{تصور}} — \emph{taṣawwara} — \textquotedblleft{}to conceive\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{لم} \ar{أتصور} \ar{أن} \ar{الرحلة} \ar{طويلة} \ar{إلى} \ar{هذا} \ar{الحد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{lam ataṣawwar anna ar-riḥla ṭawīla ilā hādhā al-ḥadd.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I did not imagine the journey was this long.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يتصور}, \emph{yataṣawwar}.

The noun \ar{تصور}, \emph{taṣawwur}, an idea, a conception.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تصور}} (\emph{taṣawwara}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ṣ-w-r}, \textquotedblleft{}to form, to shape\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form V of the root of \emph{ṣūra}, \textquotedblleft{}a picture\textquotedblright{}: to form a picture in the mind.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taṣawwara}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taṣawwara}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lam ataṣawwar anna ar-riḥla ṭawīla ilā hādhā al-ḥadd.} — I did not imagine the journey was this long.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to infer, then the Arabic for to realize, then say \emph{taṣawwara} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{تصور} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To conceive\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{استوعب} (istawʿaba)}{استوعب (istawʿaba)}]{\ar{استوعب} (istawʿaba) — to grasp}

\label{lesson:AR-C367-istawaba}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to realize, then the Arabic for to conceive.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{استوعب}}
\textbf{\ar{استوعب}} — \emph{istawʿaba} — \textquotedblleft{}to grasp\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{لم} \ar{يستوعب} \ar{الطلاب} \ar{الدرس} \ar{الأول}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{lam yastawʿib aṭ-ṭullāb ad-dars al-awwal.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The students did not take in the first lesson.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يستوعب}, \emph{yastawʿib}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{استوعب}} (\emph{istawʿaba}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{w-ʿ-b}, \textquotedblleft{}to take the whole of\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form X, to take a thing in whole: to grasp it fully.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{وعي} (waʿy)}{وعي (waʿy)}]{\ar{وعي} (waʿy) — awareness}

\label{lesson:AR-C367-way}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to conceive, then the Arabic for to grasp.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{وعي}}
\textbf{\ar{وعي}} — \emph{waʿy} — \textquotedblleft{}awareness\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{عند} \ar{الشباب} \ar{وعي} \ar{كبير} \ar{بالصحة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ʿinda ash-shabāb waʿy kabīr bi-ṣ-ṣiḥḥa.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Young people have great awareness of health.
\end{quote}

\ar{فقد} \ar{وعيه}, \emph{faqada waʿyahu}, he lost consciousness.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{وعي}} (\emph{waʿy}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{w-ʿ-y}, \textquotedblleft{}to retain, to keep in mind\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Waʿy} is the verbal noun of \emph{waʿā}, \textquotedblleft{}to hold in mind\textquotedblright{}: awareness.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{waʿy}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{waʿy}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ʿinda ash-shabāb waʿy kabīr bi-ṣ-ṣiḥḥa.} — Young people have great awareness of health.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to conceive, then the Arabic for to grasp, then say \emph{waʿy} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{وعي} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Awareness\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{معرفة} (maʿrifa)}{معرفة (maʿrifa)}]{\ar{معرفة} (maʿrifa) — knowledge}

\label{lesson:AR-C367-marifa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to grasp, then the Arabic for awareness.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{معرفة}}
\textbf{\ar{معرفة}} — \emph{maʿrifa} — \textquotedblleft{}knowledge\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{الكتب} \ar{طريق} \ar{إلى} \ar{المعرفة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{al-kutub ṭarīq ilā al-maʿrifa.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Books are a road to knowledge.
\end{quote}

Plural \ar{معارف}, \emph{maʿārif}, also acquaintances.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{معرفة}} (\emph{maʿrifa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ʿ-r-f}, \textquotedblleft{}to know\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Maʿrifa} is a verbal noun of \emph{ʿarafa}, \textquotedblleft{}to know\textquotedblright{}: knowledge, knowing.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}
